title: Cyclotomic dot annihilators, finite-dimensional blocks, and finite root strings
statement: Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)–(Q4) for a real symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree $\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the resulting ordinary quotient. Every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic annihilator in each fixed block, every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over $k$, and, for fixed $\beta,i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.
strategy:
Use the exact native presentation, and abbreviate its globally opposite source crossing by $\kappa_a=-\tau_a$ for every color pair; the dots, idempotents and $Q$ do not change. For equal adjacent colors put $x=x_a,y=x_{a+1}$ and $\partial f=(s_af-f)/(x-y)$. If $fe(\nu)$ annihilates a module, the source nil-Hecke identities give $(x-y)\kappa_a f\kappa_a e(\nu)=(s_af-f)\kappa_a e(\nu)=(\kappa_af-\partial f-f\kappa_a)e(\nu)$. The terms containing $f$ vanish, so $\partial f$ vanishes; then $s_af=f+(x-y)\partial f$ also vanishes. This proves annihilator closure under the divided difference and exchange without division by an integer. A common monic annihilator of the first dot is $g_1=\prod_j a_j$, with the zero corners understood in the same way.

Suppose a common monic $g$ of degree $d$ annihilates $x_a$. Equal-color exchange gives $g(y)=0$. At an unequal pair $j,l$, $\kappa_ag(x)\kappa_a=g(y)Q_{jl}(x,y)=0$. Set $C=k[x]/g$, finite free of rank $d$. Multiplication by $Q_{jl}(x,y)$ on $C[y]$ has matrix $M(y)$ with leading coefficient $c\,\mathrm{Id}$ and degree $-a_{lj}$ in $y$, where $c=t_{j,l;0,-a_{lj}}\ne0$. Its determinant $r(y)$ has leading coefficient $c^d$. Applying $\operatorname{adj}(M)M=r\,\mathrm{Id}$ to the vector $1$ gives $Q_{jl}(x,y)R(x,y)\equiv r(y)\pmod {g(x)}$. Thus $g(y)r(y)$ annihilates the corner; divide its leading scalar to obtain a monic polynomial. If $d=0$ that corner is zero; if $a_{lj}=0$, $r=c^d$ is a unit. Take the product over the finite words/pairs and induct over positions. PBW then reduces each dot exponent below its monic bound, leaving finitely many permutations, words and exponent tuples, so the block is finite dimensional. This is a direct ordinary-algebra argument for arbitrary monic polynomials, including $u(u-1)$, rather than a flat-specialization claim.

For standard powers one can strengthen the bounds to nilpotence. If $x^N=0$ and the neighboring colors differ, write $Q_{jl}(x,y)=c y^q+xH(x,y)$, $q=-a_{lj}$, using homogeneity and Q4. The quadratic relation gives $y^NQ=0$, hence $y^{N+q}=-c^{-1}xy^NH$ on the corner. Raising this commuting-polynomial equality to the $N$th power gives $y^{N(N+q)}=0$. Equal-color exchange preserves the exponent $N$. Starting with a common first-strand power proves nilpotence of every dot.

For finite root strings in either branch fix a prefix length $\ell$ and a common monic annihilator $g$ of degree $d$ for $x_{\ell+1}$ in the finite length-$\ell+1$ quotient. Its image annihilates that dot in every longer quotient, since right concatenation preserves the first-strand ideal. In an all-$i$ tail of length $d+1$ starting at position $\ell+1$, repeated annihilator closure gives $\partial_{\ell+d}\cdots\partial_{\ell+1}g(x_{\ell+1})=(-1)^d$, so the tail is zero. Equivalently, in native nil-Hecke rank $s>d$, multiply $g(x_1)$ by $x_1^{s-1-d}x_2^{s-2}\cdots x_{s-1}$. Its top term is the Artin staircase and its lower terms have smaller total degree; the native $\partial_{w_0}$ sends it to $1$. Thus $\partial_{w_0}$ and the full staircase idempotent belong to the ideal generated by $g$. The finite matrix units from the perfect Artin pairing put $1$ in that ideal. Both computations use unit diagonal elimination, never $s!^{-1}$.

Finally induct on the number $b$ of non-$i$ entries. Let $k=L_{b-1}$ be the previous bound and $\ell=b-1+k$. Choose an all-$i$ tail bound $m$ at that prefix length and set $L_b=k+m-1$. A word of length $b+L_b=\ell+m$ with at least $L_b$ copies of $i$ either has at least $k$ in its first $\ell$ positions, whose prefix is already zero, or has at most $k-1$ there and therefore all last $m$ positions are $i$. That tail is zero. A longer word with at most $b$ other colors has a zero initial segment of length $b+L_b$. For fixed $\beta$, $b=\sum_{j\ne i}\beta_j$, so $\beta_i+m\ge L_b$ kills every word in $\beta+m\alpha_i$. The prefix never has to end in color $i$. All constructions involve finite products, determinants, polynomial reductions and integer choices.

title: Minimal-parabolic diagrams have a faithful PBW and bubble normal form
statement: Fix a color $i$. In the formal graded minimal-parabolic proof category of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], the reduced perfect-matching diagrams, dot monomials on their open components, and monomials in the independent far-left normalized $i$-bubble coefficients form a basis of every morphism space. In particular, at all-downward boundaries of weight difference $\beta$, the morphism space is the corresponding KLR PBW corner tensored with the polynomial ring in one positive bubble family; the opposite/fake family is its coefficientwise reciprocal. The graded polynomial flag models of [[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]], with universal monic framing and arbitrarily large auxiliary framing at each fixed physical source weight, are jointly faithful. The assertion is about this formal proof category before cyclotomic quotient transfer.
strategy:
Use $\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for all colors. The formal category's relations are the exact model-verified local equations: downward KLR, both rank-one triangles, cyclic dots, rho/cross-and-cap equations and bubble inversion, mixed cap/cup equations, and the finite-coefficient bubble slides. For an $i$ root $x$, its normalized bubble series changes by $(1-xt)^{\pm2}$; for a spectator $j$ root $y$ it changes by $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)^{\pm1}$, where $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$ has constant coefficient $1$. These are verified directly because the model series is $p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2$, adjoining an $i$ root multiplies $c_r$ by $u-x$, and adjoining a spectator multiplies $p$ by $Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$. Every fixed inverse coefficient is a finite polynomial recursion. These slides are specified formal relations checked on the model; deriving a slide from the faithfulness being proved is not used.

To span, move dots to fixed component positions with cyclicity and KLR dot moves. An equal-color correction has one fewer crossing. Sort each $i$ cup/cap toward a boundary or the far-left closed-component position using the specified mate equations. A main term passes one of its finitely many crossing obstacles; a correction term removes an unsorted open-component extremum or such an obstacle. Rank-one cross-and-cap sums are finite: open dot counts are nonnegative and negative-degree bubbles vanish, bounding the indices at a fixed total degree. Adjacent opposed cup/cap pairs cancel by the triangles. Induct on the lexicographic pair of unsorted extrema and remaining crossing obstacles, and on crossing length for correction terms. Closed components have color $i$; cancel extra extrema, slide them left by the finite coefficient equations, and express the reverse family by bubble inversion. Coxeter deletion and KLR braid/quadratic straightening then reduce each open matching to the selected reduced diagram, with all braid defects shorter. This yields the stated finite span. At all-downward boundaries every open arc joins bottom to top, hence is a colored permutation; the reduced matching and its dots are exactly a PBW monomial. For general boundaries the two triangles give invertible Hom correspondences bending the upward $i$ endpoints to the other boundary, and the same straightening has unit leading matching coefficients.

For independence hold the physical source weight $\mu$ fixed and write $\mu_i=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$. Choose fixed nonnegative spectator background counts $m_j$ and let $A_{\rm spect}=\sum_{j\ne i}(-a_{ij})m_j$. For an increasing background $i$ count $r$, set $N=\mu_i+2r$ and $\lambda_i=N-A_{\rm spect}$. These equations keep the physical weight $N-2r=\mu_i$ fixed. Only $i$ dominance is needed, since the model has no spectator upward generator; one may take all $m_j=0$. Use the universal graded monic framing $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}+z_1u^{\lambda_i-1}+\cdots+z_{\lambda_i}$ with independent $\deg z_a=2d_i a$. Put $p=a_i\prod Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $c_r=\prod(u-x_a)$. The correct normalized series is $\mathcal B(t)=p^{\rm rev}/(c_r^{\rm rev})^2=a_i^{\rm rev}U(t)$, $U_0=1$. Its coefficient $\mathcal B_a=z_a+\sum_{1\le\ell<a}z_\ell U_{a-\ell}+U_a$ is unit triangular in the framing variables. The reciprocal family's coefficient is $-z_a$ plus lower framing indices. Thus the first $D$ bubble coefficients are independent whenever $\lambda_i\ge D$, even in characteristic two and at negative physical weight. No claim of a unit old-root coefficient is made: $\mathcal B_1=p_1+2e_1$ can lose its root term in characteristic two.

A nonzero finite PBW/bubble combination remains nonzero after that triangular substitution over the independent polynomial coefficient domain. The generic KLR polynomial representation has a distinct nonzero leading permutation for each selected crossing word; choose a polynomial test vector with nonzero output, clearing a finite denominator if needed. Let $D$ bound the bubble indices and let $B$ bound the actual internal degrees of that vector and its output; both are finite and are determined in the untruncated polynomial ring. Let $L$ bound the number of added $i$ flags in the tested words. Every monic flag relation and factor-ring coefficient relation after those flags has degree at least $2d_i(N-r-L+1)=2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)$; spectator appends can only increase $N$. All coefficient and root variables are nonnegatively graded and all dot degrees are positive. Choose $r\ge0$, $\lambda_i\ge D$, and $2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)>B$, also making any finitely required background root count large enough. Such an integer exists while $\mu$ is fixed. The ideal generated by the homogeneous model relations cannot meet degrees at most $B$, so the nonzero PBW output survives in that flag model. This is exact degree separation, not a deformation-flatness inference. The model's ordered word shifts, $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$ with $i$ last, make every crossing homogeneous of degree $-b_{jk}$; the polynomial witness is checked before its overall word shift. The formal upward generator is $H_i=E_i^{\rm basic}\{-d_i(1+h_{\rm input})\}$, not unnormalized restriction, so its spectator commutators are truly degree zero. Hence the faithful underlying witness is also a witness in the specified graded model.

The downward spanning map is therefore injective. The finite unit-triangular bending change then gives independence for the full matching family. Specializing the far-left bubble variables acts only on that tensor factor in the downward normal form; no ordinary KLR relation appears from coefficient evaluation alone. Universal grading is used only to witness formal faithfulness; subsequent inhomogeneous monic field specialization is governed by the separately proved algebraic cap-off kernel.

title: Coherent cyclotomic graded biadjunction and crossing mates

Put $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda- etaangle$ and $t_i( eta)=2d_i(1-h)=(\alpha_i|\alpha_i)-2(\Lambda- eta|\alpha_i)$. There are explicit homogeneous bimodule units and counits with both triangle identities giving $E_i\{t_i( eta)\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ on all graded module categories. They preserve the standard dot-cyclic and same-color crossing-mate identities and the coherent different-color double-mate identity: for $p_

The corresponding arbitrary monic field quotients have the same underlying ungraded biadjunction and ordered crossing-mate identities after forgetting internal shifts. No Frobenius, integral Grothendieck-module or crystal theorem is a premise.
strategy:
Work throughout with $\kappa=-\tau_{\rm native}$ for every color pair. This is a graded algebra isomorphism preserving $Q$ and all first-strand monic ideals: quadratic relations have two signs, the braid defect three, and $\kappa_w=(-1)^{\ell(w)}\tau_w$. Hence model crossings are native $-\pi$ and $-Q$; changing only equal-color crossings is not allowed. Use the formal category and its explicit graded flag model from the declared suppliers. With $i$ last in a total color order, raw downward flags have shifts $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$. A degree-$D$ raw map between word shifts $S,T$ has degree $D+T-S$. Thus a source increasing crossing $\pi$ of degree zero and its reverse multiplier $Q$ of degree $-2b_{jk}$ both have actual degree $-b_{jk}$. Basic $E_iG_j$ has the prescribed $-b_{ij}$ shifted commutation. Formal $H_i=E_i^{\rm basic}\{-d_i(1+h_{\rm input})\}$ cancels that shift: $h$ increases by $-a_{ij}$ under $G_j$ and $s_j(m-e_i)=s_j(m)+b_{ij}$. It is formal $H_i$, rather than basic $E_i$, that commutes unshiftedly with the spectator flag.

At a vertex with $r$ i roots and total monic degree $N$, put $L=C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]/(\text{factor coefficients above }N-r)$, $c_r=\prod(u-x_a)$, $p=a_i\prod Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $b=p/c_r$. The i-flag algebra is $B=L[z]/b(z)$, free over the old ring on powers $0\le j<N-r$ and free over the target root-append ring on powers $0\le j\le r$. The two coefficient traces $\tau_{\rm old}$ and $\tau_{\rm new}$ extract the respective top powers in their monic remainders. Their Gram matrices in power/complementary bases are triangular with diagonal one, so they have explicit dual bases without factorial denominators. Basic $F_i=B\{-2d_i r\}\otimes-$ and basic reverse $E_i=B\otimes-$ use $\tau_{\rm new}$ and its dual bases for the first adjunction and $\tau_{\rm old}$ for the second. If $(u_a,v_a)$ are either pair of dual bases, the unit is $1\mapsto\sum_av_a\otimes u_a$ and the counit is its coefficient trace. The identities $\sum_av_a\tau(u_ax)=x$ and $\sum_a\tau(xv_a)u_a=x$ give both triangles directly. The trace-degree difference is $-2d_i(N-2r-1)=t_i(\beta)$. Source second maps are normalized by $(-1)^{N+1}=(-1)^{h+1}$, with the unit given the inverse scalar; degree-zero bubbles are one. Transporting $\kappa=-\tau$ preserves these maps and triangles, and dots/crossings inherit their actual pairing-adjoint identities.

For coherent mixed maps, let $Q_{ij}(u,y)=t_{ij}q(u,y)$ with $q$ monic and replace $p$ by $pq$. The successive i/j flags have rings modulo $b$ and $bq$; their source crossings are quotient $\pi$ and multiplication by $Q$. Monic coefficient extraction gives $\epsilon_{pq}(Qf)=t_{ij}\epsilon_p(f)$ on the one-variable power basis. On all nil-Hecke matrix entries use the ordered residue form $t_r^p(z)=(-1)^{r(N-r)}\operatorname{Res}(\Delta_r b_r\operatorname{Tr}(z)/\prod_s p(X_s))$, with $\Delta_r=\prod_{s<t}(X_s-X_t)$ and $b_r=X_1^{r-1}\cdots X_{r-1}$. It equals the integral parabolic divided-difference form: summing ordered distinct roots gives $\Delta^2$, repeated roots vanish, and the resulting integral polynomial identity specializes to every characteristic. There is no $1/r!$. For $U_r=\prod_sQ_{ij}(X_s,y)$, cancellation gives $t_r^{pq}(U_rz)=(-1)^{r(-a_{ij})}t_{ij}^r t_r^p(z)$. Perfect coefficient pairings then give the full relative identity $\pi_r\widehat\epsilon^{pq}(Q(X_{r+1},y)\operatorname{lift}z)=t_{ij}\widehat\epsilon^p(z)$ after the global second-map normalization; it holds for every matrix/coset element. Its ordinary mate is the mixed-unit identity. Native single crossings add one minus sign, while the two-sideways composites have two and retain $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$. Their ordered quotient is $t_{ji}/t_{ij}$ for the i strand running SW–NE. This proves the formal crossing-mate relation without assuming a one-dimensional Hom space.

Transfer that formal relation to the actual first-strand quotient using the declared cap-off kernel supplier and PBW/bubble normal form, not rank-one detection of arbitrary map equality. Let $J$ be generated by $H_iv_\Lambda$ and $a_j(x)G_jv_\Lambda$. The marked i generator closed with dot powers forces $H(t)a_i^{\rm rev}(t)=1$; its canonical unit columns $x^k\eta$, $k<\lambda_i$, have companion polynomial exactly $a_i$. Genuine vacancy loops have index $\lambda_i+1+s$ and vanish, whereas the lower fake coefficients in the monic branch are retained. Every factor through a vacuum $H_i$ bends to an added first i strand. The cap-off supplier proves the full two-double-coset PBW reduction: no first crossing closes to that zero loop; one first crossing must be equal-color and its actual cross-and-cap sum is a unit sign times $a_i(x)$, with decorated value $a_i(x)P(x,x)$. Physical exterior factors commute with closure. Arbitrary upward whiskers of a marked $a_j$ reduce by input naturality of the mixed maps/rho; for negative h use the actual retract $\iota=\rho^{-1}j_{EF}$, $\pi=p_{EF}\rho$, $\pi\iota=1$. The branch reaching the marker is zero by the companion matrix when j=i or by mixed dot commutation and $H_iv=0$ otherwise. The finite word-object induction treats every marked whisker and every factor map. Thus $J$ meets the downward corner in exactly the ordinary first-strand ideal.

The algebraic right-append kernel agrees explicitly. Set $K_0=Se(\beta,i)/Sa(x_1)R(\beta)e(\beta,i)$ and $K_1=Se(i,\beta)/Sa(x_2)R_1(\beta)e(i,\beta)$. PBW makes them finite right $R^a(\beta)[t]$-projectives. Right multiplication $P=a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_n$ is bilinear; its counterpart $Q=g_n\cdots g_1$ uses the source intertwiners and satisfies $QP=\sum_\nu a_i(t)\prod_{\nu_a\ne i}Q_{i\nu_a}(t,x_a)e(\nu)$, with a unit leading scalar. Hence P is injective. The full-transfer PBW coset gives $\operatorname{im}P=\ker(K_0\to R^a(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i))$; shorter cosets lie in the prefix ideal. This is also valid ungraded for arbitrary monic $a_j$. It identifies the formal quotient's word corners with the actual cyclotomic corners in dependency order. All quotient objects are summands of finite sums of negative words: move formal H through the last downward letter by mixed commutation or the sign-correct EF retract and induct on word length, starting from $H_iv=0$. Thus the idempotent-completed formal quotient is the category of actual word projectives. Right appending is the actual induction, and its first adjoint is actual basic restriction by tensor-Hom uniqueness; the rho/dot formulas fix the second maps coherently under this same identification.

Finally evaluate each formal unit/counit on the regular algebra, which is the finite sum of word idempotent projectives. Naturality with its homogeneous right multiplications (and shifts) makes each evaluated map a homogeneous bimodule map. Their two triangle identities on the regular objects are equalities of those bimodule maps. Tensoring them with any graded module therefore gives units/counits with the same triangles on all graded modules, not only word projectives. The crossing-mate equality similarly is an equality of bimodule maps and extends by tensoring. Forget the internal degrees after arbitrary inhomogeneous monic coefficient specialization; all monic, dual-basis, residue, companion, cap-off and kernel identities remain algebraic identities. No graded highest-weight action is inferred for that deformation. At every stage the finite-dimensional/root-string supplier and projectivity/commutator suppliers are algebraic prerequisites; a symmetric/Frobenius or Grothendieck/crystal theorem is never used.
